subject: GGIR version 1.11-0 on CRAN and new release structure

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: GGIR version 1.11-0 on CRAN and new release structure
parts:
Dear GGIR-users,

GGIR version 1.11-0 is now on CRAN, new updates are listed in the change log. Thanks Matt for enhancing the visual report, thanks Jairo for assisting with a few of the other updates, and thanks to all of you who reported issues.

New release structure
So far I have created a new GGIR release with every significant improvement to GGIR. This resulted in 18 releases in the past two years. This is not very practical. 

From now onward I aim to reduce the number of CRAN releases to only two or three per year, and to create intermediate releases on GitHub only. New features and bug fixes will first be released on GitHub, which creates a time window for identifying and fixing bugs before they end up in the next CRAN release.

This will make CRAN releases more stable and a good starting point for new GGIR users, while GitHub releases will become the place for the latest bug fixes and feature additions.

If possible, please use the GitHub version whenever you can to help spot issues timely before they end up in a CRAN release. 

With this new release structure I will use the following version coding.
A.B-C 
A only increases with major changes that affect backward compatibility with previous releases.
B increases with every CRAN release
C increases with every GitHub release.

So, the next GitHub release will be 1.11-1, while the next CRAN release will be 1.12-0 integrating all 1.11-x GitHub releases.

To install GGIR from GitHub, do from within R:
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("wadpac/GGIR")

or

install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("wadpac/GGIR")

To install GGIR from CRAN, do from within R:

install.packages("GGIR",dependencies=TRUE)

or use the RStudio/R toolbar for package installation.

Best wishes,

Vincent
